title: What If Fig Wasps Vanished From the Rainforest?

scenes.text: What if one wasp the size of a lowercase i vanished? A rainforest buffet goes with it.
Each fig species has just one or two wasp species that pollinate it.
The female lives only a day or two, and may fly over six miles to find the right fig.
Without her, figs can't be pollinated. Over 2,000 bird species have been recorded eating figs, plus monkeys, bats and peccaries.
Figs fruit at random times, so some fig is almost always ripe. Scientists call them keystone resources.
Figs and their wasps began together about 75 million years ago. Lose one, and an ancient partnership ends.

What if fig wasps vanished?
Figs depend on tiny wasps, and thousands of animals depend on figs.
